scenes.title: Solving x² - 4 = 0
scenes.narration: We begin with the equation x squared minus four equals zero. This is a difference of two squares, so it factorises into x minus two times x plus two. A product is zero only when one factor is zero, so x equals two or x equals minus two.

scenes.title: The graph of y = x² - 4
scenes.narration: Here is the graph of y equals x squared minus four. Notice that it crosses the x axis at exactly the two roots we found, minus two and two.

scenes.title: Solutions on a number line
scenes.narration: On the number line, the inequality x squared minus four is less than zero holds for x strictly between minus two and two. The open circles show that the endpoints are not included.

scenes.title: A triangle and its circle
scenes.narration: Finally, a geometric picture. Triangle A B C has vertices A, B and C. The circle centred at A passes through B, so every point on it is the same distance from A.
